title: WHAT IS GIVEN TO GOD IS HOLY

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"'If what they vowed is an animal that is acceptable as an offering to
the LORD, such an animal given to the LORD becomes holy. They must not
exchange it or substitute a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a
good one; if they should substitute one animal for another, both it and
the substitute become holy'" - Lev 27:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Once an animal was vowed to the Lord, it was His. You could not later
have second thoughts and quietly swap it for a weaker one from your
flock. And if you tried, God's response was striking: now He owned both.

This closes a very human loophole. In the heat of gratitude a person
might promise God his best animal, then later look at it and think, "That
one is too valuable — let me give a lesser one instead." God does not
allow the downgrade. What is given to Him stays given.

Dear reader, we are all tempted to renegotiate with God once the
emotional moment has passed. We promise Him our time, then reclaim it
when we get busy. We surrender an area of our life, then quietly take it
back. We offer Him our best, then substitute our leftovers.

Paul urges us to offer our bodies as a living sacrifice (Rom 12:1), and
the trouble with a living sacrifice, someone has observed, is that it
keeps trying to crawl off the altar.

What have you given to God and then quietly taken back? He is not looking
to trap you, but He does call you to integrity. Let your surrender be
real. What you have placed in His hands, leave in His hands.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have I given to God and then quietly reclaimed?
2. Where am I tempted to substitute my leftovers for my best?
3. What would genuine, unreserved surrender look like for me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, forgive me for taking back what I have given You. Help me leave
in Your hands what I have surrendered, and to give You my best without
second thoughts. Amen.
